mainTopic: Is a woman believed that the man she was with was of fit lineage? This leads to the refutation of רב אסי, the status of her daughter, and the meaning of שתוקי.
overview: The amud opens with the end of a source about a woman seen going off with a man to a hidden place or a ruin. She says he was a כשר כהן. רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר believe her, and רבי יהושע does not without proof. The גמרא asks why, according to רב אסי, the source lists two places. It concludes that the two cases are a ruin in the city and a ruin in the field, and that each one is needed. A ברייתא then records a back-and-forth between רבי יהושע and the חכמים, comparing this woman to a captive woman. Read properly, the ברייתא treats the 'speaking' woman and the pregnant woman as two separate cases, which refutes רב אסי. The גמרא learns from the ברייתא that the majority of people nearby does not decide this dispute, which supports רבי יהושע בן לוי. רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר then argue about whether the daughter's status follows the mother's. This leads to שמואל's case, which shows that a שתוקי can be fit and is only kept from כהונה. The amud ends by starting a story of an engaged couple before רב יוסף, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The case of the woman seen going into a ruin with a man
steps.stepSummary: The source ends its case: the woman says the man was a כהן and her cousin. רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר believe her. רבי יהושע does not believe her without proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or she was seen going into a ruin with a man. People asked her, 'Who is this man?' She said, 'He is a כהן, and he is my father's brother's son.' רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר say she is believed. רבי יהושע says we don't decide our lives by what she says. She keeps the status of a woman who was with a נתין or a ממזר until she brings proof for her words.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quoted source about a woman seen going with a man into a hidden place or a ruin. It gives the argument over whether we believe her that the man was כשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that she had relations with a man who would make her unfit to marry a כהן. רבן גמליאל trusts her claim that he was a כשר כהן. רבי יהושע holds that she is assumed to be unfit until she proves otherwise.

keyTerms.meaning: A ruin, an abandoned broken building where people can be alone
A descendant of the גבעונים, who is not allowed to marry into כשר families
A child born from a forbidden union, also not allowed to marry into כשר families

phrases.english: or into a ruin —

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרוּ לָהּ: מָה טִיבוֹ שֶׁל אִישׁ זֶה?
phrases.english: and they said to her: What is the nature of this man?

phrases.aramaic: כֹּהֵן הוּא, וּבֶן אֲחִי אַבָּא הוּא.
phrases.english: He is a priest, and he is the son of my father's brother.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמְרִים: נֶאֱמֶנֶת,
phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Eliezer say: She is believed,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: לֹא מִפִּיהָ אָנוּ חַיִּין,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says: We do not live by her mouth,
phrases.notes: He means we don't base our decisions only on her word.

phrases.english: rather, she is in the presumed status of one who had relations
with a Netin or a mamzer,
until she brings proof for her words.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ לְחוּרְבָּה — וְאָמְרוּ לָהּ: מָה טִיבוֹ שֶׁל אִישׁ זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a source quoted just before this point, which the גמרא is about to examine
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר: she is believed that the man was כשר. רבי יהושע: she is assumed unfit until she brings proof.

steps.title: Why list two places according to רב אסי?
steps.stepSummary: For זעירי, listing both סתר and חורבה makes sense. For רב אסי, who says the argument is only about a woman who had relations, two cases seem extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for זעירי: that is why the source teaches two cases, a hidden place or a ruin. But for רב אסי, who said the case means she had relations, why do I need two?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests this source against an earlier argument. זעירי explained the משנה's word 'talking' as 'secluded', and רב אסי explained it as 'had relations'. The גמרא asks why, according to רב אסי, the source lists two places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For זעירי, the argument applies even to plain seclusion. So listing a hidden place (smaller worry) and a ruin (bigger worry) teaches something new. For רב אסי, the argument is only where she clearly had relations, so the two places seem to say the same thing.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out well for (one opinion), but...

phrases.english: Granted, according to Ze'eiri —
that is why it teaches two:
into seclusion or into a ruin.
But according to Rav Asi, who said 'she had relations,'
why do I need two?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the source from step 1 to challenge רב אסי
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's explanation that the argument is about a woman who had relations
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the case is relations, a hidden place and a ruin lead to the same result, so listing both looks extra.

steps.title: It is one case: the hidden part of a ruin
steps.stepSummary: For רב אסי, the source describes only one place: the secluded area of a ruin.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches one case: into the seclusion of a ruin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רב אסי that the words are not two separate cases. They describe one place, a hidden spot inside a ruin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'סתר' and 'חורבה' together describe one place, nothing is extra. A hidden spot in a ruin is where people go to have relations, which fits רב אסי's view.

phrases.english: It teaches one:
into the seclusion of a ruin.
phrases.notes: The answer reads the words as 'the hidden spot OF a ruin' instead of 'a hidden spot OR a ruin'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two separate places are listed, so one is extra for רב אסי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only one place is meant: the hidden part of a ruin.

steps.title: But the text says 'or'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects that answer, because the source clearly says 'seclusion OR a ruin'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it teaches 'into seclusion or into a ruin'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last answer. The word 'או' (or) shows that two separate cases are listed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reading 'the hidden spot of a ruin' does not fit the actual wording. So the original question about רב אסי comes back.

phrases.english: But it teaches 'into seclusion or into a ruin'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 3
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole answer that only one case is meant
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word 'או' clearly separates two cases.

steps.title: Two kinds of ruins: in the city and in the field
steps.stepSummary: New answer for רב אסי: both cases are ruins. One is a ruin in the city and one is a ruin out in the open field.
steps.simpleTranslation: One is about a ruin in the city, and one is about a ruin in the field.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer for רב אסי. The two cases really are two, but both are ruins, one inside the town and one outside it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This keeps the word 'or' as two cases. It also fits רב אסי, since both are places where relations would happen. The difference between them is who is likely to be around.

keyTerms.meaning: A ruin out in the open field

phrases.english: One for a ruin of the town,
and one for a ruin of the field.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲדָא לְחוּרְבָּה דְמָתָא, וַחֲדָא לְחוּרְבָּה דְּדַבְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 3 and answers step 2 again
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two cases are a hidden place and a ruin, which is extra for רב אסי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The two cases are a city ruin and a field ruin.

steps.title: Why the field ruin is needed
steps.stepSummary: If we only had the city ruin, we might think רבן גמליאל believes her only because most people nearby are כשר. In a field ruin, where most people nearby are פסול, he might agree with רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both are needed. If it only taught a city ruin, I would say רבן גמליאל declares her fit there because most people near it are כשר. But in a field ruin, where most people near it are פסול, I would say he agrees with רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts proving that both cases are needed (צריכותא). This first half shows why the field ruin had to be taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is 'majority' (רוב). Near a city ruin, most people are of good lineage, which supports her claim. Near a field ruin, most people passing by are not, so we might think even רבן גמליאל would not believe her. Teaching the field case shows that he believes her even there.

keyTerms.meaning: Declares her fit (to marry a כהן)
People unfit to marry into כשר families

phrases.english: And both are needed, because if it taught us only a ruin of the town —
in this case Rabban Gamliel declares her fit,
because the majority near it are of fit lineage.
But for a ruin of the field,
where the majority near it are unfit —
I would say he agrees with Rabbi Yehoshua.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up step 5 by showing the field case teaches something new
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The field case teaches that רבן גמליאל believes her even where most people nearby are פסול.

steps.title: Why the city ruin is needed, so both are needed
steps.stepSummary: If we only had the field ruin, we might think רבי יהושע doubts her only there. In a city ruin he might agree with רבן גמליאל. So both cases are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it only taught that case (the field ruin), I would say רבי יהושע only says she is not believed there. But here (in a city ruin), I would say he agrees with רבן גמליאל. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the צריכותא from the other side and concludes that both cases are needed. This answers the question that step 2 raised against רב אסי, so his view survives for now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Teaching the city case shows that רבי יהושע does not believe her even where most people are כשר. Each case shows how far one side goes: רבן גמליאל believes her even in the field, and רבי יהושע doubts her even in the city.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed (both cases are needed)

steps.whatToRemember: For רב אסי, the source's two cases are a ruin in the city and a ruin in the field. Each is needed: רבן גמליאל believes her even in the field, where most people are פסול. רבי יהושע doubts her even in the city, where most people are כשר.

phrases.english: And if it taught us only that one —
in that case Rabbi Yehoshua says (she is not believed),
but in this one —
I would say he agrees with Rabban Gamliel,
so it is needed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן בְּהָהִיא — בְּהָהִיא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the second half of the צריכותא begun in step 6
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both cases are needed. This answers the question of step 2 for רב אסי.

steps.title: A challenge from a ברייתא: is the woman believed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. In it, the חכמים say a woman is believed about herself, and רבי יהושע says she is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא raises a challenge: This is testimony that a woman is fit for, and רבי יהושע says she is not believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The word מיתיבי tells us the גמרא is bringing a ברייתא to challenge what came before. This line sets up the ברייתא's argument, and the challenge will become clear at the end of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a woman who was with a man and says he was כשר (fit lineage). The ברייתא calls this 'testimony a woman is fit for,' meaning her own word counts. רבי יהושע disagrees and says her word alone is not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit or valid: here, her testimony counts

steps.confusionAlert: 'זו עדות שהאשה כשרה לה' does not mean the woman is כשר. It means this is a kind of testimony a woman is allowed to give. Her own word is accepted.

phrases.english: They raised a challenge:
This is testimony that a woman is fit to give,
and רבי יהושע says: she is not believed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining why the משנה needs both ruin cases, the גמרא now brings an outside ברייתא as a challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's explanation that מדברת (speaking) in the משנה means she had relations.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Once the exchange is read properly (steps 15-17), the ברייתא turns out to treat מדברת and מעוברת as two separate cases. That would make no sense if מדברת already meant she certainly had relations, as רב אסי said.

steps.title: רבי יהושע compares her to a captive woman
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע argues that the חכמים agree a captive woman who says 'I am pure' is not believed, so this woman should not be believed either.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to them: Don't you agree about a captive woman, who has witnesses that she was captured, and she says 'I am pure,' that she is not believed?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע tries to prove his view from a case the חכמים already agree to: a שבויה (captive woman).
steps.deeperAnalysis: A captive woman who says 'nothing happened to me' is not believed. רבי יהושע says this woman is the same: she says something good about herself that we cannot check, so she should not be believed.

phrases.english: רבי יהושע said to them:
Don't you agree about a captive woman who was taken captive,
and she has witnesses that she was taken captive,
and she says, 'I am pure,'
phrases.notes: She means her captors did not touch her.

phrases.english: that she is not believed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יהושע supports his opinion from step 8 with a comparison.
steps.raayaObject: The woman is not believed about the man's lineage.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The agreed case of a captive woman who claims she is pure.

steps.title: The חכמים: the captive has witnesses, this woman doesn't
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים agree about the captive but say the cases differ. The captive has witnesses that she was captured, and this woman has no witnesses against her.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Yes. But what difference is there between this and that? This one has witnesses, and that one has no witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים accept the captive rule but reject the comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the captive, witnesses already created a strong reason to suspect her. Here nobody testified to anything. She could have denied being with anyone at all, so her admission plus her claim should be trusted.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: 'Yes, indeed' (we agree), with a 'but' implied

phrases.english: They said to him: Yes, we agree.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה הֶפְרֵשׁ יֵשׁ בֵּין זוֹ לָזוֹ?
phrases.english: But what difference is there between this one and that one?
This one (the captive) has witnesses,
and that one has no witnesses.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה הֶפְרֵשׁ יֵשׁ בֵּין זוֹ לָזוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי יהושע's comparison from step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between the two cases, not the captive rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The captive has witnesses creating suspicion, while this woman has none.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: her pregnancy is her witness
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע answers that this woman also has 'witnesses,' because her pregnancy is plain to see.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: This one also has witnesses, because her belly is between her teeth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע pushes back on the חכמים' difference and says it is not real.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her pregnancy shows clearly that she was with a man. So she could not have denied it, and her admission gains her nothing. The two cases are alike again.

keyTerms.meaning: Between her teeth: a way of saying her pregnancy is very obvious

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: אַף לָזוֹ יֵשׁ עֵדִים,
phrases.english: He said to them: This one too has witnesses,
for her belly is between her teeth.
phrases.notes: A picture of a very visible pregnancy. Everyone can see she was with a man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the distinction made in step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that this woman has no witnesses.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Her visible pregnancy works like witnesses.

steps.title: The חכמים: captors are usually immoral
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים offer a new difference. Most captors are immoral, so the captive is suspect. That is not true of the man this woman was with.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Most gentiles are steeped in immorality.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים give a fresh reason why the captive is different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the captive, the people around her were mostly immoral, so we assume the worst. Here there is no such majority, so there is no strong reason to doubt her claim about who the man was.

phrases.english: They said to him:
Most gentiles are unrestrained in forbidden relations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After losing the 'witnesses' difference, the חכמים offer a new one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since both women are clearly suspect, they should be treated the same.
steps.terutzMaskana: The captive's case is special because her captors were mostly immoral.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: no one is guarded from sin
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע replies that no one has a guardian protecting them from forbidden relations, so this woman is suspect too.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: There is no guardian for forbidden relations.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע rejects the חכמים' new difference. This is his final word in the debate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Anyone can fall into this sin, so being with a man here is also suspect. Since she already lost her good standing, we cannot trust her claim that the man was כשר.

phrases.english: He said to them:
There is no guardian against forbidden relations.
phrases.notes: He means nobody is automatically safe from this temptation, so everyone is open to suspicion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the majority-based distinction of step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that only the captive's situation creates suspicion.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Anyone can sin in this area, so this woman is also suspect.
steps.whatToRemember: The debate keeps moving. The חכמים try two differences: witnesses, then 'most gentiles.' רבי יהושע knocks down each one and holds that she is no better than the captive.

steps.title: The argument is only about herself, not her daughter
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא limits the debate. It is only about the woman herself. About her daughter, everyone agrees the child is a שתוקי.
steps.simpleTranslation: When was this said? About a woman's testimony for herself. But a woman's testimony about her daughter: everyone agrees the child is a שתוקי.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends by drawing a line: the מחלוקת is only about the woman's own status. About her daughter, everyone agrees the child is a שתוקי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her word can help her own status, but about her daughter the ברייתא says everyone agrees the child is a שתוקי. רבי אלעזר will later use this line against רבי יוחנן (step 24), and the גמרא will explain what שתוקי means here (steps 25-29).

keyTerms.meaning: In what case was this said? (it introduces a limit)
A child whose father is unknown, treated with doubt about lineage

steps.confusionAlert: Don't decide yet what שתוקי means here. Whether it means the daughter is unfit is argued later: רבי אלעזר reads it that way in step 24, and the גמרא answers in step 25 that a שתוקי can be fit.
steps.whyThisMatters: This agreed limit becomes the basis of רבי אלעזר's challenge to רבי יוחנן in step 24. Any view that her claim helps her daughter must deal with this ברייתא.
steps.whatToRemember: Herself: a מחלוקת. Her daughter: everyone says the child is a שתוקי.

phrases.english: In what case were these things said?
In a woman's testimony about herself,
but a woman's testimony about her daughter,
phrases.notes: She is claiming that her daughter's father is of fit lineage.

phrases.english: everyone agrees the child is a שתוקי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the ברייתא by limiting the whole debate to the woman herself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מחלוקת is only about her own status (רבן גמליאל's side believes her). About her daughter, all agree the child is a שתוקי; what that means is discussed in steps 24-29.

steps.title: The exchange does not seem to match
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי יהושע was really saying and what the חכמים were really answering, because their replies seem to talk past each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was he saying to them, and what were they answering him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops and points out that the debate in the ברייתא seems confused. It is setting up a new reading of the whole exchange.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע had answered that the pregnancy itself is like witnesses. The חכמים then switched to a different argument about immoral captors. The גמרא wants to know how these replies connect to each other.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he saying? A question asking what a statement really means.

phrases.english: What is he saying to them
phrases.notes: He means רבי יהושע, speaking to the חכמים in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: and what are they answering him?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָאָמַר לְהוּ וּמַאי קָמַהְדְּרִי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how the arguments in steps 10-13 fit together.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the replies of רבי יהושע and the חכמים connect to each other.

steps.title: The חכמים move from the pregnant woman to the 'speaking' woman
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים accept רבי יהושע's answer about the pregnant woman. They then ask him about a woman who was only seen speaking with a man.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what they were saying to him: You answered us about the pregnant woman. What will you answer us about the woman who was speaking with a man?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the חכמים changed the case. They accepted his point about the pregnant woman and challenged him with the 'speaking' woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pregnant woman obviously had relations, so her pregnancy works like witnesses. A woman who was only seen speaking with a man has no proof of relations at all. That is why the חכמים raise this case next.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who was seen 'speaking' with a man.

phrases.english: This is what they are saying to him:
You answered us about the pregnant woman.
What will you answer us about the 'speaking' woman?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15 by re-reading the exchange as moving from the pregnant case to the 'speaking' case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חכמים conceded the pregnant case and moved on to challenge him with the 'speaking' case, where there is no proof of relations.

steps.title: The rest of the debate read as being about the 'speaking' woman
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע says the 'speaking' woman is like the captive. The חכמים say captors are different because most are immoral. רבי יהושע replies that she was secluded with a man, and no one is guarded from forbidden relations.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: The speaking woman is the same as the captive. They said to him: A captive is different, because most gentiles are immoral. He said to them: This one too, since she secluded herself with a man, there is no guardian against forbidden relations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now fits the rest of the debate into this new reading. Every reply is about the 'speaking' woman, not the pregnant one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this reading the debate flows smoothly. There is real doubt whether the 'speaking' woman had relations, so the 'immoral captors' argument makes sense. רבי יהושע answers that being alone with a man is enough to suspect her.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who was taken captive.
She secluded herself, meaning she was alone with a man.
There is no guardian against forbidden relations. No one can be trusted to hold back.

phrases.english: He said to them: The 'speaking' woman is the same as a captive.
They said to him: A captive is different,
because most gentiles are immoral.
He said to them: This one too,
since she secluded herself with a man,
there is no guardian against forbidden relations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the re-reading from step 16 and fits steps 12-13 into the 'speaking' case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second half of the debate is about the 'speaking' woman, where there is real doubt, so the 'immoral captors' argument and the reply fit.

steps.title: Two separate cases refute רב אסי
steps.stepSummary: The re-reading shows the ברייתא has two separate cases, 'speaking' and pregnant. That refutes רב אסי, who said 'speaking' means she had relations.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any event, it teaches two cases: speaking and pregnant. This is a refutation of רב אסי. It is indeed a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the new reading to knock down רב אסי's explanation. It ends with a final refutation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי explained that 'speaking' in the משנה is a polite way of saying she had relations. The ברייתא treats 'speaking' as a separate case from pregnancy, where relations are certain. So 'speaking' must mean she was only seen talking with him, and רב אסי's reading cannot stand.

keyTerms.meaning: In any event; at least this much is clear.
A refutation. When it is said twice, it means a final refutation.

steps.whatToRemember: 'Speaking' (מדברת) means she was only seen talking or alone with a man, not that she certainly had relations. רב אסי's view is rejected.

phrases.english: In any event, it teaches two cases —
speaking and pregnant.
A refutation of רב אסי!
phrases.notes: Earlier on the daf, רב אסי explained that 'speaking' means she had relations with the man.

phrases.english: It is indeed a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the result of the re-reading in steps 16-17 against רב אסי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's explanation that מדברת means she had relations.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists מדברת and מעוברת as two different cases. If מדברת already meant certain relations, it would be the same as the pregnant case.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב אסי is refuted. מדברת is a case of doubt.

steps.title: Why not use the difference of who is around her?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא did not give a simpler difference: around the captive most men are unfit, while around this woman most men are fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it derive the difference from this: there, most men around her are unfit, and here, most men around her are fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's choice of arguments. It suggests a more obvious reason to tell the captive apart from this woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The captive is surrounded by gentiles, who are unfit for a כהן. A woman in her own town is surrounded mostly by Jews of good lineage. If the majority counts, this alone should have been enough to separate the cases, so why bring other arguments?

keyTerms.meaning: Let him derive it from this; why not give this simpler reason?
Most men are unfit for a כהן's family.
Most men are fit, of good lineage.

phrases.english: But let it derive it from this:
that there, most men around her are unfit,
phrases.notes: 'There' is the captive, who is among gentiles.

phrases.english: and here, most men around her are fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the ברייתא chose the 'immoral captors' difference instead of a majority-based one.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's choice of how to tell the captive apart from the secluded woman.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A simpler difference exists, based on whether most men around her are fit or unfit, yet the ברייתא does not use it.

steps.title: Support for רבי יהושע בן לוי: the majority does not matter here
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's silence supports רבי יהושע בן לוי. In his view, the one who declares her fit does so even when most men are unfit, and the one who declares her unfit does so even when most men are fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רבי יהושע בן לוי, who said: According to the one who declares her fit, he does so even when most are unfit. According to the one who declares her unfit, he does so even when most are fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. The ברייתא did not use the majority argument because, in this dispute, the majority does not decide the outcome. That fits רבי יהושע בן לוי's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל believes her claim even when the men around her are mostly unfit. רבי יהושע doubts her even when they are mostly fit. Because both sides ignore the majority, the ברייתא could not use it as a difference, and that backs רבי יהושע בן לוי.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who declares her fit, meaning רבן גמליאל.
The one who declares her unfit, meaning רבי יהושע.

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the dispute is about whether we trust her claim, not about which men are the majority around her.

phrases.aramaic: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי.
phrases.english: This supports רבי יהושע בן לוי.
For רבי יהושע בן לוי said:
According to the one who declares her fit —
phrases.notes: That is רבן גמליאל, who believes her claim.

phrases.english: he declares her fit even when most are unfit,
according to the one who declares her unfit —
he declares her unfit even when most are fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19 by showing the majority argument is not relevant here, which supports רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule that the majority does not affect either side of the dispute.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The fact that the ברייתא did not use the majority-based difference between the captive and the secluded woman.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the daughter follows the mother
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that whoever declares the woman fit also declares her daughter fit, and whoever declares her unfit also declares her daughter unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: According to the one who declares her fit, he declares her daughter fit. According to the one who declares her unfit, he declares her daughter unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: A new discussion begins about the daughter born from this relationship. רבי יוחנן says the daughter's status matches the mother's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבן גמליאל, trusting the mother's claim that the man was of good lineage makes the daughter fit as well. For רבי יהושע, both mother and daughter are unfit.

phrases.english: רבי יוחנן said:
According to the one who declares her fit —
he declares her daughter fit.
According to the one who declares her unfit —
he declares her daughter unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לְדִבְרֵי הַמַּכְשִׁיר בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a discussion of the daughter's status, which step 14 had raised.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The daughter's status follows the mother's on both sides of the dispute.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: even the lenient view makes the daughter unfit
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר disagrees. Even the one who declares the mother fit declares her daughter unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: According to the one who declares her fit, he declares her daughter unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives a different view from רבי יוחנן's. In his view, even the lenient opinion does not extend to the daughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said the daughter always follows the mother. רבי אלעזר splits them: רבן גמליאל trusts the mother for herself but still treats the daughter as unfit.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two אמוראים. רבי יוחנן says the daughter follows the mother either way. רבי אלעזר says even the lenient view makes the daughter unfit.

phrases.english: And רבי אלעזר says:
According to the one who declares her fit —
he declares her daughter unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: לְדִבְרֵי הַמַּכְשִׁיר בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי יוחנן's view in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even רבן גמליאל, who declares the mother fit, declares the daughter unfit.

steps.title: רבה explains רבי אלעזר's reasoning
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains why רבי אלעזר believes the mother but not about her daughter. The mother has a חזקה דכשרות, and the daughter does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: What is רבי אלעזר's reason? It makes sense that she herself is believed, because she has a presumption of being fit. But her daughter has no presumption of being fit.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives the reason behind רבי אלעזר's view from the last step. The mother is fit and her daughter is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mother was fit before the incident, so her claim only has to keep a status she already had. The daughter was born from a doubtful union, so she never had a fit status. Her fitness would have to be proven from scratch, and the mother's word is not enough for that.

keyTerms.meaning: a presumption of being fit (for marrying a כהן)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the main principle of the argument. A claim that keeps an existing status is stronger than a claim that has to create a new status.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה, מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: Rabba said: What is the reason of Rabbi Elazar?
It makes sense that she herself
has a presumption of fitness.
Her daughter does not have a presumption of fitness.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה, מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רבי אלעזר's ruling in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The mother is believed because she has a חזקה דכשרות. The daughter has none, so the mother's claim cannot make her fit.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר challenges רבי יוחנן from a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר quotes a ברייתא. It says that when a woman testifies about her daughter, everyone agrees the child is a שתוקי. He reads this to mean the child is unfit, which goes against רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר objected to רבי יוחנן: When is this argument said? Only when a woman testifies about herself. But when a woman testifies about her daughter, everyone agrees the child is a שתוקי. Doesn't that mean a שתוקי who is unfit?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר brings a ברייתא to attack רבי יוחנן, who said the daughter is fit too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא limits the argument between רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע to the woman's own status. About the daughter, 'everyone' calls the child a שתוקי. That would mean even רבן גמליאל, who believes the mother, does not make the daughter fit. רבי אלעזר assumes that שתוקי means unfit.

keyTerms.meaning: in what case are these words said?
a 'silenced' child, whose father's identity is not known

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar objected to Rabbi Yochanan:
In what case are these words said?
In a woman's testimony about herself,
but a woman's testimony about her daughter
everyone agrees the child is a שתוקי.
Doesn't it mean a שתוקי, and unfit?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining רבי אלעזר's view to using a ברייתא against רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling (step 21) that whoever makes the mother fit also makes the daughter fit.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says 'everyone' calls the daughter a שתוקי. If שתוקי means unfit, then even the one who believes the mother does not make the daughter fit.

steps.title: A שתוקי can still be fit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן. The ברייתא means the child is a שתוקי but still fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It means a שתוקי who is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי אלעזר's reading of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word שתוקי only tells us the father's identity is unclear. It does not have to mean the child is unfit to marry. So the ברייתא does not go against רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: No: a שתוקי, and fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 24 by reading the word שתוקי differently.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading a key word in the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שתוקי means unfit, so the ברייתא goes against רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: שתוקי can describe a child who is fit, so רבי יוחנן still stands.

steps.title: Is there such a thing as a fit שתוקי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a שתוקי can really be fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there such a thing as a שתוקי who is fit?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the answer it just gave. This sets up the next step, which brings a proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually שתוקי suggests a doubtful, problem status. So the גמרא wants an example where a child is called שתוקי and is still fit.

phrases.english: And is there a שתוקי who is fit?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the answer in step 25 is possible.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where a child is called שתוקי and is still fit.

steps.title: שמואל's case of the ten כהנים
steps.stepSummary: Yes. שמואל says that if one of ten כהנים had relations with a woman, the child is called a שתוקי, even though the father is surely a fit כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, as שמואל said: If ten כהנים are standing, and one of them went off and had relations, the child is a שתוקי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with שמואל's case, where a שתוקי is clearly fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All ten men are כהנים, so whoever the father is, he is fit. The child is called שתוקי only because we don't know which of them is the father. So the name שתוקי can go along with being fit.

phrases.english: Yes, as Shmuel said.
For Shmuel said:
Ten kohanim are standing,
and one of them went off and had relations,
the child is a שתוקי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמואל's ten כהנים case: the father is surely a fit כהן, but the child is still called שתוקי.

steps.title: What does שתוקי mean in שמואל's case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks in what way this child is 'silenced.' It rejects the idea that it is about inheritance, because that would be too obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'שתוקי' mean here? If you say we silence him from his father's property, that is obvious. Do we even know who his father is?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what שתוקי means in שמואל's case. It tries one answer and rejects it, which sets up the real answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying the child cannot inherit would teach us nothing. With ten possible fathers, of course he cannot claim any one man's property. So שמואל must mean something else.

phrases.english: What does 'שתוקי' mean?
If you say that we silence him from his father's property,
phrases.notes: Meaning he has no claim to inherit from his father.

phrases.english: that's obvious!
Do we even know who his father is?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״שְׁתוּקִי״? אִילֵימָא שֶׁמַּשְׁתִּיקִין אוֹתוֹ מִנִּכְסֵי אָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the word שתוקי means in שמואל's case from step 27.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what way the child in שמואל's case is 'silenced.'

steps.title: Silenced from כהונה, based on a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The child is 'silenced' from the status of כהונה. The פסוק gives כהונה only to a כהן whose children are traced to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, we silence him from the status of כהונה, as it is written: 'And it shall be for him and his offspring after him a covenant of everlasting כהונה.' That means one whose offspring are traced to him. This leaves out this case, where the offspring are not traced to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real meaning of שתוקי in שמואל's case. The child cannot be a כהן, even though his father surely was one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links passing on כהונה to having children who are known to be the father's. Here we don't know which כהן is the father, so the child does not become a כהן. Still, nothing makes him unfit, so this is the 'fit שתוקי' that supports רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: the status of being a כהן

steps.whatToRemember: A שתוקי is not always unfit. In שמואל's case, the child is only 'silenced' from כהונה, because he cannot be traced to a specific father. So the ברייתא's word שתוקי does not go against רבי יוחנן.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't confuse 'not a כהן' with 'unfit.' This child cannot serve as a כהן, but his lineage has no flaw.

phrases.english: Rather, we silence him from the status of kehunah,
as it is written:
"And it shall be for him and for his offspring after him
a covenant of everlasting kehunah,"
one whose offspring are traced to him,

phrases.aramaic: יָצָא זֶה שֶׁאֵין זַרְעוֹ מְיוּחָס אַחֲרָיו.
phrases.english: which leaves out this one, whose offspring are not traced to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the real meaning of שתוקי after step 28 rejected the inheritance meaning.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שתוקי means silenced from כהונה, based on the פסוק requiring offspring who are traced to the father.

steps.title: An engaged couple comes before רב יוסף
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a story. An אָרוּס and his אֲרוּסָה come to רב יוסף. She says the pregnancy is from him, and his reply is about to come.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was once an engaged man and his engaged woman who came before רב יוסף. She said: "The baby is from him." And he said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new case story connected to the topic of who a child's father is. It only tells us her claim; his answer comes in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the גמרא discussed rules about a child whose father is unknown. Now it brings a real court case before רב יוסף to show these questions in practice. The key detail is her claim that the engaged man is the father. The man's answer will decide the direction of the case.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who is betrothed (קידושין done) but not yet fully married (no נישואין)
A woman who is betrothed but not yet fully married
From him; she is saying he is the father

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the story is over. The amud stops in the middle of a sentence, and the man's answer comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: There was a certain betrothed man and his betrothed woman
phrases.notes: They are formally engaged through קידושין but not yet fully married. She is pregnant.

phrases.english: who came before רב יוסף,
She said: "It is from him," and he said:

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא אָרוּס וַאֲרוּסָתוֹ דַּאֲתוֹ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defining a שתוקי and how it affects כהונה, the גמרא turns to a practical court case about a child's father.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. This step presents the case: a pregnant אֲרוּסָה claims her אָרוּס is the father, and his response is about to follow.
